clue.text: It measures inclination of worker after 31 days

indicators.note: after tells us the worker comes behind the month in the answer

parts.note: October has 31 days, abbreviated Oct
the ant is the classic worker in crosswords

explanation.surface: Somebody's mood is gauged after a month of solid work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Inclination' looks like a mood or preference, but here it is an angle, as measured by a navigational instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: An octant is an old navigator's instrument for measuring angles of elevation, like a sextant with an eighth of a circle.

clue.text: Confused underground worker in hospital

parts.note: Dis is the Roman god of the underworld, and his realm
an orderly is a hospital attendant

explanation.surface: A muddled Tube employee ends up in a hospital ward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Underground' suggests the London Tube, but DIS is the classical underworld.
explanation.definitionFit: Something disorderly is jumbled and untidy, the same as confused.

clue.text: Flower seller (American) places note in van

indicators.note: van means the front, so the note is placed at the head of the seller

parts.note: la is the sixth note of the sol-fa scale
vender is the American spelling of vendor, a seller

explanation.surface: A US florist puts a musical note in their delivery van.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Van' looks like a vehicle, but it means the vanguard or front, so 'places ... in van' puts LA ahead of VENDER; 'places' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Lavender is a fragrant purple-flowered shrub, an example of a flower.

clue.text: Artist — one in European city

indicators.note: in places the numeral inside the painter's name

parts.note: Edvard Munch, the Norwegian painter of The Scream
the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: A painter is said to be living in a city on the Continent.
explanation.definitionFit: Munich is the capital of Bavaria in Germany, an example of a European city.

clue.text: Suspect "spray" precedes "decay"

indicators.note: precedes means the first word's synonym goes before the second's

parts.note: a mist is a fine spray of droplets
rust is the corrosion or decay of iron

explanation.surface: A cryptic note about aerosols coming before rot.
explanation.definitionFit: To suspect someone is to distrust or doubt them, a synonym as a verb.

clue.text: Exasperated expression: "A loss?"

definitions.meaning: the weary cry when something bad happens yet again
read cryptically, a loss is the absence of a gain

explanation.surface: Someone sighs in irritation at yet another loss.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is the stock groan of exasperation, and also literally describes a loss as the opposite of a gain.

clue.text: European city — not one cooking pasta

parts.note: Riga is the capital of Latvia

indicators.note: cooking suggests the letters are being worked up into something new

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: In some Continental city, nobody is cooking pasta.
explanation.walkthrough: The dash splits the surface; 'European city' is wordplay here, while 'cooking' signals the shuffle of NOT and the numeral to give TONI.
explanation.definitionFit: Rigatoni are short ridged tubes, a kind of pasta.

clue.text: Cream leaving castle in Scotland, it's said

indicators.note: leaving means the cream's synonym departs from the castle's name

parts.note: Balmoral is the royal family's castle in Aberdeenshire, Scotland
a balm is a soothing cream or ointment

explanation.surface: An ointment is taken away from a Scottish castle, so people say.
explanation.walkthrough: BALMORAL is the British royal family's Scottish holiday castle. 'It's said' looks like a homophone signal, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Oral means spoken rather than written, so something oral is said aloud.

clue.text: Feature a couple

definitions.meaning: a single article or point in a list or a newspaper
two people romantically linked, in informal use

explanation.definitionFit: An item is a feature or entry in a list, and informally a pair who are dating are said to be one.

clue.text: Pasta recipe created for tyrant

indicators.note: created suggests the letters are being made into a new form

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for recipe, from Latin recipe meaning take

explanation.surface: A pasta recipe is invented for a despot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'created' rearranges PASTA plus R.
explanation.definitionFit: A satrap was a Persian provincial governor, and by extension any petty despot or tyrant.

clue.text: Tyrant is held back by reputation, but gains first title

indicators.note: is held means the reversed emperor sits inside the reputation

parts.note: fame is renown or reputation

indicators.note: back means the emperor's name is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: Nero was the notoriously tyrannical Roman emperor

explanation.surface: A despot is restrained by his reputation, yet still acquires a top title.
explanation.walkthrough: The emperor's name turned round gives OREN, which 'is held' places inside the reputation word; 'by' and 'but gains' are links, and 'first title' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A forename is the given name that comes before the surname, so the first of a person's names.

clue.text: Title: "Took offence … just"

parts.note: a title is a legal right or entitlement to property
minded, as in minding something, means objected to or took offence

explanation.surface: A heading reading 'took offence' followed by a trailing 'just'.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Title' means a legal claim to something, as in title to land, hence RIGHT.
explanation.definitionFit: Right-minded people have sound moral principles, so they are just and fair.

clue.text: "I have rights!", priest groans — first one charged with atheism

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for right, so two rights give RR
Eli is the Old Testament priest who brought up Samuel

indicators.note: first picks out only the opening letter of groans

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one is I
on means live or switched on, as a charged circuit is

explanation.surface: A man insists on his rights, and the clergyman sighs that this first one is charged with godlessness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'have' and 'with' are links. ELI is the biblical priest.
explanation.definitionFit: Irreligion is the lack of religious belief, a near synonym for atheism.

clue.text: Volumes of moving water raised by ten points

indicators.note: raised in a down clue means the word is read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: the tide is the regular movement of the sea
ten written as the digits 1 and 0 looks like the letters I and O
N and S are compass points, north and south

explanation.surface: Books written about tidal flow increased by ten points.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' turns TIDE upwards in this down clue to give EDIT; 'by' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Editions are versions or printings of a book, so volumes in a looser sense.

clue.text: Big bird once upon a time mixed grit with seed

definitions.text: Big bird once upon a time

indicators.note: mixed suggests the letters of the two words are stirred together

explanation.surface: Some giant bird long ago ate grit mixed with seed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mixed' rearranges GRIT and SEED; 'with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Estridge is an obsolete word for the ostrich, the largest bird, hence 'once upon a time'.

clue.text: Just in Germany, clutching cocktail

indicators.note: clutching means the words before it hold the answer within their letters

explanation.surface: Someone in Germany is just holding on to a cocktail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Just' looks like an adverb meaning only, but its last letters start the answer, which runs on through 'in Germany'.
explanation.definitionFit: A stinger is a cocktail of brandy and crème de menthe.

clue.text: Rotten logs have split

indicators.note: rotten suggests something decayed and fallen apart, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Decaying timber has cracked apart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'split' looks like what happens to rotting timber, but it is the definition, meaning to share.
explanation.definitionFit: To go halves is to share a cost equally, splitting it between two people.

clue.text: Cocktail of red and rosé mixed on screen

indicators.note: mixed suggests the two wines are blended, so their letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A drink made by mixing red and rosé wine is served on a screen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mixed' rearranges RED and ROSE; 'Cocktail of', 'and' and 'on' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: A reredos is an ornamental screen behind a church altar.

clue.text: Screen actress, a prickly one to watch

parts.note: holly is a shrub with prickly leaves
a hunter is a pocket watch with a hinged cover

explanation.surface: A film star is described as a spiky character worth keeping an eye on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to watch' looks like an instruction to view, but HUNTER is a kind of watch.
explanation.definitionFit: Holly Hunter is an Oscar-winning American film actress, star of The Piano.

clue.text: Cheerful if parts of mug exchanged

indicators.note: exchanged means the two parts of the phrase swap places

parts.note: to mug someone is to beat them up

explanation.surface: Someone becomes happier when the pieces of a cup are swapped round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mug' suggests a cup, but it is the verb: BEAT UP, whose two halves change places; 'if parts of' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Upbeat means optimistic and positive in mood, a synonym for cheerful.

clue.text: Smart bird ditches bloke

indicators.note: ditches means the man's name is dropped from the bird

parts.note: a chicken is a farmyard bird
Ken is a man's name, standing for any bloke

explanation.surface: A stylish girlfriend dumps her man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Smart bird' wants to be a fashionable woman (British slang 'bird'), but 'Smart' is the definition and the bird a chicken.
explanation.definitionFit: Chic means fashionable and stylish, as smart does of dress.

clue.text: Far East takes in a quarter

indicators.note: takes in means the letters are found within the phrase that follows

explanation.surface: The Orient includes a district of its own.
explanation.definitionFit: A quarter of a town is a district, and an area is a region or district.

clue.text: Watch hole, or go out?

indicators.note: out suggests the letters are disordered or wrong

explanation.surface: A question whether to keep an eye on a gap or leave.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges HOLE, OR and GO.
explanation.definitionFit: A horologe is an archaic word for a timepiece such as a clock or watch.

clue.text: Out with a woman

parts.note: broad is American slang for a woman

explanation.surface: Going on a date with a lady.
explanation.walkthrough: BROAD is old American slang for a woman; 'with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Abroad can mean out of doors or out and about, as in news being abroad.

clue.text: Woman supervising child, animal and man

parts.note: an ape is an animal
Ron is a man's name

explanation.surface: A lady looks after a youngster, a pet and a gentleman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'and' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A chaperon is an older woman who accompanies and supervises a young unmarried woman.

clue.text: Man holding dipstick left with hound

indicators.note: holding means the man's pronoun surrounds the other pieces

parts.note: he is the pronoun for a man
dipstick is slang for an idiot, an ass

explanation.surface: A man with a measuring rod departs with his dog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dipstick' suggests an engine's oil gauge, but here it is slang for a fool; 'with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To hound someone is to pester or harass them, as to hassle them.
